cmux relays Claude Code commands into tmux panes.

Claude cannot type into its own terminal, but it can run a shell command, and a
shell command can tell tmux to type. That is all cmux is.

Usage:
  cmux [flags] <command> [arguments]

Commands:
  goal <text>         Set the target session's goal
  compact             Compact the target's conversation
  clear               Clear the target's conversation
  prompt <text>       Send the target a plain message
  restart <text>      Wait for the turn to end, clear, then send a first prompt
  model <name>        Switch the target's model
  resume              Open the target's resume picker
  rate-limit-options  Arm the target to wait out a usage limit and carry on
  watch               Wait out usage limits on a pane, unattended
  context             Show the target's context usage
  cost                Show the target's cost and usage
  agents              Open the target's agent list
  interrupt           Cancel whatever the target is doing
  mcp <subcommand>    Manage the target's MCP servers
  panes               List the Claude Code panes cmux can see
  status              Show this pane, detection result and default target

Flags:
  --to <target>      pane id (%12), session:window.pane, or an index from cmux panes
  --all-panes        allow a target that was not detected as Claude Code
  --dry-run          print the tmux calls instead of making them
  --defer <seconds>  have tmux deliver the keys later, via run-shell
  --self             allow interrupt to target the pane cmux was run from
  -h, --help         show help
  --version          show version

Examples:
  cmux goal Ship the parser rewrite
  cmux compact
  cmux panes
  cmux --to %12 interrupt
  cmux --defer 5 clear

Notes:
  Slash commands take effect immediately, even if the target is mid-turn. That
  includes clear and compact, so aiming one at your own pane discards history
  while your turn is still running. Use --defer to get out of the way first.

  interrupt is different again: it sends a bare Escape, which is never queued
  and cancels the target's current turn on arrival.

Run 'cmux <command> --help' for more about one command.
